requestedparts.evaluation: Complete: Starting money: 25. The raw answer supplies this fact semantically, and the cited frozen-summary passage supports it. No fact was borrowed from another answer.
requestedparts.observedanswerquote: Each player starts with 25 money, 1 active association worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers lying below it. Draw 8 Zoo cards, keep 4 and discard 4; draw 2 Final Scoring cards. All five Action cards start side I; Animals goes in the leftmost slot, and the other four are randomized among the remaining slots. Appeal starts at 0 for the first player, then 1, 2 and 3 in turn order.

summarysupportquote-or-line.quote: - **B.** Take one set of Action cards (Build, Cards, Animals, Association, Sponsors). Place one card **side I up** under each of the five card slots on your zoo map: the **Animals** card under the leftmost slot (showing 1), the remaining 4 randomly under the other slots.

- **C1.** Place your appeal, conservation, and reputation counters on the first spaces of their tracks. On the **Appeal track**, stagger by turn order: start player on space 0, second player on space 1, third on space 2, fourth on space 3.
- **C3.** Place 1 association worker on the notepad of your zoo map (the active worker) and the remaining 3 lying down on the designated spaces below the notepad.
- **D.** Take 25 money and put it on your notepad.
- **E.** Draw 2 Final Scoring cards and place them next to your zoo map. You may look at them at any time, but keep them hidden from other players.

- **F.** Draw 8 Zoo cards; keep 4 as hand cards and discard the other 4 to a face-up discard pile on the board. Keep hand cards hidden. (Tip from the rulebook: choose 1–2 Sponsor and 2–3 Animal cards without conditions you cannot fulfill early, ideally matching the Base Conservation Projects on display.)

requestedparts.observedanswerquote: After a slot-4 card is used, remove it, shift cards from slots 1–3 one slot right, and put the used card in slot 1. Set strength before acting; each X-token spent adds 1 strength, returns to supply, and cannot exceed 5 held. X-tokens gained during the action cannot boost it. Resolve an ‘after finishing’ effect after completing the action, including the card movement.

summarysupportquote-or-line.quote: On your turn, choose one of your 5 Action cards, shift it lower than the others to show it is in use, and perform its action with the strength of its card slot (1 = far left through 5 = far right; the further right, the more powerful). After completing the action, remove the card from its slot, shift all Action cards left of the now-empty slot one slot to the right, and place the used card in slot 1.

**X-tokens.** You may use X-tokens to increase an action's strength: each token spent adds +1 strength, then returns to the supply. You may spend any number in one action (for some actions, strength above 5 no longer improves the action). You can never hold more than 5 X-tokens. Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps of that action; resolve its items one at a time. You must pay each item before receiving its own benefits. You set the strength **before** performing the action — X-tokens gained while performing an action cannot boost that same action.
**"After finishing" effects.** If a card effect says "after finishing" your action, complete the action — including moving the Action cards — before executing the effect.

requestedparts.observedanswerquote: When the Break token reaches its last space, ignore movement beyond it and the player who reached it gains 1 X-token. Finish the current turn, then conduct the break; play resumes clockwise with the next player after the break. The summary does not describe a break itself as granting extra turns; extra turns are part of the separate game-end rule.

summarysupportquote-or-line.quote: **The Break track.** At the start of the game and after each break, the Break token sits on the starting space for your player count. Various actions and card effects advance it toward the end of the track. When it reaches the **last space**, you call a break for everyone: the break takes place after the end of your current turn, and you get **1 X-token** for reaching the last space. Ignore any additional steps beyond the last space. After the break, the token returns to its starting space.
6. **Break track:** return the Break token to the starting space for your player count. Play then continues clockwise with the next player.

"I" means an instant benefit on playing; "R" a recurring trigger; "B" break income; "F" final scoring. Effects referring to icons count the card itself. Unless an effect says "any zoo," use your own zoo. All X-token gains obey the five-token limit. For animal sizes, **small** means printed standard size 1 or 2, including Petting Zoo animals; **large** means size 4 or 5. Size 3 is neither.

requestedparts.part: Cards I: move break two, then deck draws under its table or one display snap
requestedparts.evaluation: Complete: Cards I: move break two, then deck draws under its table or one display snap. The raw answer supplies this fact semantically, and the cited frozen-summary passage supports it. No fact was borrowed from another answer.
requestedparts.observedanswerquote: Cards I advances the Break token 2 spaces, then either draws from the deck per the card's strength table (up to 3, possibly discarding) or, at strength 5+, snaps exactly 1 display card of any reputation without a deck draw. Cards II also advances 2; draw from the deck and/or from cards within reputation range, in any order, using its table. A side-II snap works at strength 3+ and takes exactly 1 card of any reputation, with no deck draw. Cards II display cards are not replenished until turn end; Cards I snap is also replenished at turn end. There is no in-turn hand limit; discard to the limit only at breaks.

summarysupportquote-or-line.quote: - **Side I:** Advance the Break token **2 spaces** (you do not gain money for this). Then either **draw from the deck** — compare the strength of the slot with the table on the card and draw the indicated number of cards (maximum 3), after which you might have to discard a card from your hand (one just drawn or one already held) — or **snap**: with strength **5 or more**, instead take exactly **1 card of your choice from the display** into your hand, regardless of your reputation. Replenish the display at the end of your turn. There is no in-turn hand limit; you only discard to your limit during breaks.

- **Side II:** Advance the Break token 2 spaces, then draw cards from the deck **and/or from within reputation range** (the display up to your Reputation counter), in any order, using the upgraded table on the card (e.g., at strength 5 you take 4 cards and discard 1). The display is not replenished until your turn is complete. Snapping now works from strength **3** (strength above 3 makes no difference to a snap). **On either side, snapping takes exactly one display card of any reputation, with no deck draw; the reputation restriction applies only to the side-II draw option, not snapping.** Upgrading the Cards action also lets you progress **past 9 reputation** on the Reputation track.
- **Hand size:** unlimited during play; enforced only at breaks (limit 3, or 5 with the specific university).

requestedparts.part: Build I: exactly one building of size no greater than strength
requestedparts.evaluation: Complete: Build I: exactly one building of size no greater than strength. The raw answer supplies this fact semantically, and the cited frozen-summary passage supports it. No fact was borrowed from another answer.
requestedparts.observedanswerquote: Build I builds exactly 1 building of size up to strength; Build II builds any number of different buildings with total size no greater than strength, never two identical buildings in one action. Each costs 2 money per space. Your first building must have at least one space on a map border; later buildings must touch an existing building by an edge. Build only on empty spaces and not over water or rock; restricted-icon spaces require Build II. Kiosks must be at least 3 spaces apart. Each pavilion gives 1 appeal when placed.

summarysupportquote-or-line.quote: - **Side I:** Build **exactly 1 building** of your choice, of size up to the action's strength. Pay **2 money per space** (cost = size × 2) into the supply before placing. Available: kiosk (size 1), pavilion (size 1), standard enclosures (sizes 1–5), and the Petting Zoo (special enclosure, size 3; maximum 1 per zoo — other buildings can be built more than once).

- **Placement rules:** build adjacent to an existing building (at least 1 edge touching); your **first building** must instead have at least 1 space on a border space of your zoo map. Build only on empty spaces; buildings may not extend beyond the map, overlap buildings, or cover water/rock spaces. Spaces with the restricted icon require the upgraded Build action. A kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk (at least 2 spaces between kiosks). If you cannot legally build the desired building, you must choose a different building. Build standard enclosures **empty side up** (yellow edge, showing the size); the Petting Zoo is the same on both sides. Covering a placement-bonus space grants that bonus immediately, once. Each pavilion immediately (and only once) increases your zoo's appeal by 1; kiosks grant income in every break; enclosures house animals.

- **Side II:** Build **as many different buildings as you like** with a **maximum total size equal to the strength** — but never 2 identical buildings in the same Build action. Newly available: **Large Bird Aviary** and **Reptile House** (special enclosures, both size 5, maximum 1 each per zoo, both sides the same). When you build the Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary you may immediately — and only once per building — move **all suitable animals that fit** from standard enclosures into it, choosing separately for each. Build the buildings one after the other, paying for each separately before placing it; take placement bonuses before building the next building, but hold "after finishing" bonuses until the whole Build action is complete. Side II also lets you build on the restricted-icon spaces, so you can completely cover your zoo map: if you cover every space except water and rock spaces (by any effect, not just the Build action), immediately gain **7 appeal**. Unique buildings can never be built with this action — they only come into play via their Sponsor cards.

Available: kiosk (size 1), pavilion (size 1), standard enclosures (sizes 1–5), and the Petting Zoo (special enclosure, size 3; maximum 1 per zoo — other buildings can be built more than once).

- **Placement rules:** build adjacent to an existing building (at least 1 edge touching); your **first building** must instead have at least 1 space on a border space of your zoo map. Build only on empty spaces; buildings may not extend beyond the map, overlap buildings, or cover water/rock spaces. Spaces with the restricted icon require the upgraded Build action. A kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk (at least 2 spaces between kiosks). If you cannot legally build the desired building, you must choose a different building. Build standard enclosures **empty side up** (yellow edge, showing the size); the Petting Zoo is the same on both sides. Covering a placement-bonus space grants that bonus immediately, once. Each pavilion immediately (and only once) increases your zoo's appeal by 1; kiosks grant income in every break; enclosures house animals.

- **Side II:** Build **as many different buildings as you like** with a **maximum total size equal to the strength** — but never 2 identical buildings in the same Build action. Newly available: **Large Bird Aviary** and **Reptile House** (special enclosures, both size 5, maximum 1 each per zoo, both sides the same). When you build the Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary you may immediately — and only once per building — move **all suitable animals that fit** from standard enclosures into it, choosing separately for each. Build the buildings one after the other, paying for each separately before placing it; take placement bonuses before building the next building, but hold "after finishing" bonuses until the whole Build action is complete. Side II also lets you build on the restricted-icon spaces, so you can completely cover your zoo map: if you cover every space except water and rock spaces (by any effect, not just the Build action), immediately gain **7 appeal**. Unique buildings can never be built with this action — they only come into play via their Sponsor cards.

requestedparts.part: Earlier money/cards/newly active workers may fund later steps in the same action
requestedparts.evaluation: Complete: Earlier money/cards/newly active workers may fund later steps in the same action. The raw answer supplies this fact semantically, and the cited frozen-summary passage supports it. No fact was borrowed from another answer.
requestedparts.observedanswerquote: Bonuses gained earlier in an action—including money, cards and newly activated workers—may be used for later steps of that action, but each item must be paid before receiving its own benefits. Immediate effects resolve as they occur; ‘after finishing’ waits until the entire action and Action-card movement are complete. The owning player chooses the order of simultaneous effects.

summarysupportquote-or-line.quote: **X-tokens.** You may use X-tokens to increase an action's strength: each token spent adds +1 strength, then returns to the supply. You may spend any number in one action (for some actions, strength above 5 no longer improves the action). You can never hold more than 5 X-tokens. Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps of that action; resolve its items one at a time. You must pay each item before receiving its own benefits. You set the strength **before** performing the action — X-tokens gained while performing an action cannot boost that same action.
**"After finishing" effects.** If a card effect says "after finishing" your action, complete the action — including moving the Action cards — before executing the effect.
- **Multiple simultaneous effects** (appeal, reputation, conservation points, card abilities): the owning player chooses the order of execution.

requestedparts.part: Meet all Animal-card conditions
requestedparts.evaluation: Complete: Meet all Animal-card conditions. The raw answer supplies this fact semantically, and the cited frozen-summary passage supports it. No fact was borrowed from another answer.
requestedparts.observedanswerquote: For each Animal, meet all left-side conditions and pay its printed cost first. A partner zoo on its continent reduces the cost by 3 per continent icon on that Animal, so two matching icons reduce it by 6. Standard housing requires one empty enclosure at least the required size, then flip the whole enclosure occupied; it normally holds one animal. Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo. Eligible reptiles/birds may instead use a Reptile House/Aviary, marking the indicated number of spaces with supply player tokens; special enclosures never flip and can be shared if capacity remains. Meet any required distinct adjacent water/rock hexes; count hexes, not touching edges. Immediate effects resolve before the next animal; after-finishing effects wait until the Animals action and card movement are complete.

summarysupportquote-or-line.quote: 1. **Check conditions** (left side of the card — e.g., a specific partner zoo, animal category, or continent icons). You may only play the card if you fulfill all conditions.

2. **Pay the cost** (upper-left corner) into the supply. A partner zoo on the animal's continent reduces the cost by **3 money per continent icon on the card**. Effects that gain you money for playing the animal pay out later — you must be able to pay the full cost first.

3. **Fill an empty enclosure:** any animal except Petting Zoo animals can go on its own into an empty **standard enclosure** of at least the required size (hexagon number); flip the enclosure to its occupied side. Some animals additionally require the enclosure to be next to one or two water and/or rock spaces. Count distinct adjacent hexes: multiple edges touching the same water hex still count as only one, and a larger water area counts only the hexes actually adjacent. Petting Zoo animals go **only** in the Petting Zoo. All reptiles and some birds can instead go in their special enclosure (Reptile House / Large Bird Aviary) — such cards show both enclosure requirements and you choose (water/rock requirements apply to the special enclosure too). To house an animal in a special enclosure, mark the number of spaces shown on the card with player tokens from your supply; if not enough free spaces remain in the special enclosure, it cannot go there. Special enclosures are never flipped.

5. **Execute effects:** advance your Appeal counter by the amount shown; some animals also give conservation points or reputation. "After finishing" effects wait until the entire Animals action is done; all other effects execute immediately, even before playing another Animal card (likewise effects on other cards triggered by the play). If multiple effects are simultaneous, you choose the order.

- When playing 2 animals, complete all steps for the first (except "after finishing" effects) before the second; you may decline to play a second. Execute "after finishing" effects only after moving the Animals card to slot 1.

summarysupportquote-or-line.quote: Only **immediately when a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary is built**, you may relocate all corresponding eligible animals that fit, choosing each animal separately. Check the new special enclosure's terrain adjacency and available capacity. For each animal:

requestedparts.part: Task strengths: reputation two, partner three, university four, project five
requestedparts.evaluation: Complete: Task strengths: reputation two, partner three, university four, project five. The raw answer supplies this fact semantically, and the cited frozen-summary passage supports it. No fact was borrowed from another answer.
requestedparts.observedanswerquote: Task strengths are reputation 2, partner zoo 3, university 4 and conservation project work 5. Association I performs exactly one task; Association II performs one or more different tasks whose total value is no greater than strength. Each task needs an active worker; if one of your workers is already on that task, you must place 2 workers, and if 3 are there you cannot repeat it until after the break. Other players' workers do not matter.

summarysupportquote-or-line.quote: - **Side I:** Perform **exactly one association task**. You need at least 1 active association worker: place it on the chosen task on the Association board. If 1 of your workers is already on that task, you must place **2** workers instead; if 3 of your workers are already there, you cannot perform it again until after the break. Other players' workers on a task do not matter. Each task has a strength number: your action's strength must be **at least** the task's strength.
- **Increase reputation (strength 2):** increase your zoo's reputation by **2**, taking any track bonuses you reach.

- **Gain partner zoo (strength 3):** take a partner zoo from the Association board onto the lowest empty partner-zoo space of your map (take any printed bonus immediately). All your partner zoos must be from different continents, maximum 4 total; the third (or fourth) requires the upgraded Association action. requestedparts.observedanswerquote: With Association I, either support a project already in play or play one from hand and support it immediately; Association II also permits playing a new project from the display within reputation range for its folder-number cost. To support, meet an unoccupied condition and place one of your left-edge zoo-map tokens on it. A reward level is unavailable if any player has a token there; each level holds one token total, and normally you may support each project only once. Choose a token from the left edge; its bonus activates immediately, before or after the project reward at your choice. A new project goes leftmost above the Association board, shifting others right; if over the player-count limit (2/3/4), discard the rightmost and return its tokens to owners' supplies. Activated map bonuses remain activated.

summarysupportquote-or-line.quote: - **Conservation project work (strength 5):** either support a conservation project already in play, or play a Conservation Project card from your hand and support it immediately. A new card goes on the leftmost space above the Association board, pushing existing cards one place right. Depending on player count there can only be up to 2, 3, or 4 cards above the board (e.g., 3 with three players); if the new card exceeds the limit, discard the rightmost card and return any player tokens on it to their owners' supplies (not to their zoo maps). The Base Conservation Projects below the board are never moved, even when fully supported, and no new base projects are added during the game.

- **Two separate support limits:** a reward level is available only if **no player at all** has a token on it. Each level can hold **one token total across all players**. Separately, you normally may support a particular project only once, even if another level is free. Thus an opponent's token blocks that level too; having no token of your own on the level is insufficient.

- To **support** a project: fulfill a condition on the card that has no player token on it, and place 1 player token of your choice from the left edge of your zoo map on that condition. You may support each project only **once** (never one already holding your token). As a reward, advance your Conservation counter (and Reputation counter, if shown) per the depicted award. If you fulfill several conditions, you choose one. Taking a token off your zoo map activates its bonus — gained immediately, and for some bonuses again in each break; you choose whether to take it before or after the project reward.

**Your zoo map:** buildings go in the large central area. You may not build on rock and water spaces (some animals need an enclosure next to rock or water). A built-on space is "covered." Spaces with a special icon may not be built on until you upgrade your Build Action card. Some spaces show a **placement bonus**, gained immediately when you cover them. The left edge holds the 7 player tokens used to support conservation projects (each grants a bonus when taken — always immediately, and some again in each break). The bottom has 5 card slots for your Action cards; the number above each slot is that card's strength. The right side has spaces for partner zoos (5 continents exist, but you can partner with a maximum of 4 — the third requires an upgraded Association action) and universities (3 different ones); fill each column bottom-up and take any bonus printed on a space you cover immediately. Workers, money, and X-tokens live on the notepad.

- **Side II:** Perform **one or more different** association tasks with one action (1 or 2 of your workers per task, as above). The **total value** of the tasks may not exceed your action's strength (it may be less). Tasks resolve in sequence: workers or other bonuses gained from an earlier task may be used on a later task in this same action. When doing conservation project work you may also play the new Conservation Project card directly **from the display** (within reputation range, paying the folder number as an additional cost; no replenish until turn end). In addition you may make exactly **1 donation**: pay the smallest amount of money still visible in the donation area, cover that space with a player token from your supply, and gain **1 conservation point**. The printed donation costs are **2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10**, then the repeatable **12-money** space; skip spaces blocked at setup. Once all spaces but the last are covered, each subsequent donation costs **12 money** (no further tokens placed). A donation requires having performed at least 1 association task in the same action, needs no worker, and is limited to 1 per Association action.
- **Discarded conservation projects:** tokens on a project card pushed off the display return to the owners' **supply**, not to the bonus spaces on their zoo maps (the bonuses stay activated).

To support, meet an unoccupied condition and place one of your left-edge zoo-map tokens on it. A reward level is unavailable if any player has a token there; each level holds one token total, and normally you may support each project only once. Choose a token from the left edge; its bonus activates immediately, before or after the project reward at your choice. A new project goes leftmost above the Association board, shifting others right; if over the player-count limit (2/3/4), discard the rightmost and return its tokens to owners' supplies. Activated map bonuses remain activated.

summarysupportquote-or-line.quote: - **Conservation project work (strength 5):** either support a conservation project already in play, or play a Conservation Project card from your hand and support it immediately. A new card goes on the leftmost space above the Association board, pushing existing cards one place right. Depending on player count there can only be up to 2, 3, or 4 cards above the board (e.g., 3 with three players); if the new card exceeds the limit, discard the rightmost card and return any player tokens on it to their owners' supplies (not to their zoo maps). The Base Conservation Projects below the board are never moved, even when fully supported, and no new base projects are added during the game.

- **Two separate support limits:** a reward level is available only if **no player at all** has a token on it. Each level can hold **one token total across all players**. Separately, you normally may support a particular project only once, even if another level is free. Thus an opponent's token blocks that level too; having no token of your own on the level is insufficient.

- To **support** a project: fulfill a condition on the card that has no player token on it, and place 1 player token of your choice from the left edge of your zoo map on that condition. You may support each project only **once** (never one already holding your token). As a reward, advance your Conservation counter (and Reputation counter, if shown) per the depicted award. If you fulfill several conditions, you choose one. Taking a token off your zoo map activates its bonus — gained immediately, and for some bonuses again in each break; you choose whether to take it before or after the project reward.

**Your zoo map:** buildings go in the large central area. You may not build on rock and water spaces (some animals need an enclosure next to rock or water). A built-on space is "covered." Spaces with a special icon may not be built on until you upgrade your Build Action card. Some spaces show a **placement bonus**, gained immediately when you cover them. The left edge holds the 7 player tokens used to support conservation projects (each grants a bonus when taken — always immediately, and some again in each break). The bottom has 5 card slots for your Action cards; the number above each slot is that card's strength. The right side has spaces for partner zoos (5 continents exist, but you can partner with a maximum of 4 — the third requires an upgraded Association action) and universities (3 different ones); fill each column bottom-up and take any bonus printed on a space you cover immediately. Workers, money, and X-tokens live on the notepad.

- **Side II:** Perform **one or more different** association tasks with one action (1 or 2 of your workers per task, as above). The **total value** of the tasks may not exceed your action's strength (it may be less). Tasks resolve in sequence: workers or other bonuses gained from an earlier task may be used on a later task in this same action. When doing conservation project work you may also play the new Conservation Project card directly **from the display** (within reputation range, paying the folder number as an additional cost; no replenish until turn end). In addition you may make exactly **1 donation**: pay the smallest amount of money still visible in the donation area, cover that space with a player token from your supply, and gain **1 conservation point**. The printed donation costs are **2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10**, then the repeatable **12-money** space; skip spaces blocked at setup. Once all spaces but the last are covered, each subsequent donation costs **12 money** (no further tokens placed). A donation requires having performed at least 1 association task in the same action, needs no worker, and is limited to 1 per Association action.

requestedparts.observedanswerquote: The animal's printed standard-enclosure size must match the release band: 2− means size 1 or 2, 3 means size 3, and 4+ means size 4 or 5; the occupied tile size/capacity does not set the band. Discard the Animal and lose its printed appeal and icons, but keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects already earned. Lose the appeal before gaining project conservation. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not. If the animal can live in a special enclosure and its required tokens can be removed, you must remove them; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure satisfying all requirements, or fallback to the smallest meeting size alone, or flip none if no occupied enclosure meets size. This applies to flock animals too.

summarysupportquote-or-line.quote: - **Release into the wild** projects work differently: instead of counting icons, discard 1 Animal card with the specific icon from your zoo; match the animal’s **printed standard-enclosure requirement to the depicted size category**: **2− accepts size 1 or 2; 3 accepts size 3; 4+ accepts size 4 or 5**. You cannot use an animal from another category. The actual enclosure tile occupied, or capacity in a special enclosure, does not define this category. First lose only the animal's printed appeal, **before** gaining conservation points; discard the animal and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects already earned. If the animal could live in a special enclosure and its indicated number of special-enclosure tokens can be removed, you **must remove those tokens**; only otherwise flip a standard enclosure. Flip the smallest occupied standard meeting all requirements, else the smallest meeting size alone, else none if no occupied enclosure meets size. This applies even to flock animals. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not.

requestedparts.observedanswerquote: Sponsors I plays exactly 1 card from hand if strength is at least its level and all conditions are met. Sponsors II may play one or more cards if strength +1 is at least their total levels; cards can come from hand or from display within reputation range, paying the folder number extra. Resolve cards sequentially, completing each instant effect before the next; defer after-finishing effects until the action ends. Alternatively, Sponsors I advances the Break token by strength and gives that much money even if fewer spaces remain; Sponsors II gives double that money.

summarysupportquote-or-line.quote: - **Side I:** Play **exactly 1 Sponsor card** from your hand: the action's strength must be at least the card's **level**, and you must meet any conditions on the card's left side. Execute its instant effect and/or its recurring effect (if triggered by the card's own icon), then place it next to your zoo map. **OR:** advance the Break token a number of steps equal to the strength and take that much money — you take the full money even if the Break token doesn't need all the steps to reach the final space.

- **Side II:** Play **one or more** Sponsor cards: the action's strength **+1** must be at least the sum of the levels of all played cards (X-tokens can push strength beyond 5). Play them one after another, fully executing each card's instant effects (except "after finishing" effects) before the next. Cards may come from your hand or from the display within reputation range (paying the folder number as an additional cost; no replenish until turn end). If you instead use the action to advance the Break token, you take the money **twice**. You may also play Sponsor cards whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.

- **Display timing:** whenever you take cards from the display (snap, or upgraded Cards/Animals/Association/Sponsors plays), do not replenish it until your entire turn is complete; then slide cards down folders in order and refill from the deck. During each break the folder 1 and 2 cards are discarded before refilling.

Play them one after another, fully executing each card's instant effects (except "after finishing" effects) before the next. Cards may come from your hand or from the display within reputation range (paying the folder number as an additional cost; no replenish until turn end). If you instead use the action to advance the Break token, you take the money **twice**. You may also play Sponsor cards whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.

- **Display timing:** whenever you take cards from the display (snap, or upgraded Cards/Animals/Association/Sponsors plays), do not replenish it until your entire turn is complete; then slide cards down folders in order and refill from the deck. During each break the folder 1 and 2 cards are discarded before refilling.

requestedparts.observedanswerquote: At 2 conservation, choose an Action-card upgrade or activate an association worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or a Bonus token beside that space. The first time anyone reaches 10, all players discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile; if no one reaches 10, all discard one before scoring. Check the end at the end of your turn or during a break when your Appeal and Conservation counters enter the same scoring area or pass one another; appeal gained during another player's turn waits until your own turn end or a break. If triggered at a turn end, all other players take one more turn; if during a break, all players take one more. Each Final Scoring card can give at most 4 conservation. VP = Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area of your Conservation counter. Highest positive total wins; tie goes to most project supports, then shared victory.

summarysupportquote-or-line.quote: - **2 conservation points:** either upgrade one of your Action cards (flip it) or activate an additional association worker (take a lying worker from the lowest space below the notepad onto the notepad). Each player who reaches space 2 gets this choice.

- **5 and 8 conservation points:** take either 5 money or one of the Bonus tokens next to that space (execute immediately; a taken Bonus token is then removed from the game). The 5-money option remains even after both Bonus tokens are gone.

- **10 conservation points:** the first time any player reaches or exceeds 10, **all players** choose and discard one of their Final Scoring cards (face down under the remaining pile). If no one reaches 10 conservation points before the game ends, all players must discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins.

**End of the game.** Check **at the end of your own turn or during a break**. If your Conservation counter and Appeal counter are **in the same scoring area, or pass one another**, the end of the game is triggered. A *scoring area* is one space on the Conservation track together with the adjacent spaces on the Appeal track. Appeal gained during another player's turn (for example from Polar Bear Exhibit) waits until the end of your own turn or a break to trigger the end, unless someone else triggers it first. The triggering player completes their turn and all other players take **one more turn**; if the end is triggered during a break, **all** players take one more turn.

1. Score your Final Scoring card(s) and all your cards with the end-of-game icon. Each Final Scoring card can grant up to 4 additional conservation points (by table or text, counting your universities, the cards in front of you, and their icons); you can never gain more than **4 conservation points from a single Final Scoring card**.

2. Compute Victory Points: look at the scoring area where your Conservation counter is located and find the **lowest Appeal value in that scoring area** — this is your **Target Number**. **Victory Points = your Appeal value − your Target Number.**

3. The player with the highest positive Victory Point total wins. **Tiebreaker:** the tied player who supported the most conservation projects wins (count the player tokens removed from the left side of the zoo map). If still tied, the tied players share the victory.

requestedparts.part: Flip a chosen side-I card to side II without changing its slot
requestedparts.evaluation: Complete: Flip a chosen side-I card to side II without changing its slot. The raw answer supplies this fact semantically, and the cited frozen-summary passage supports it. No fact was borrowed from another answer.
requestedparts.observedanswerquote: Flip one chosen Action card from side I to II and leave it in its slot. Its improved action is available from your next action, but it counts as upgraded immediately for conditions. You cannot upgrade all five cards because one of the upgrade opportunities allows an alternative choice.

summarysupportquote-or-line.quote: **Upgrading Action cards.** All Action cards start on side I. When you receive a card upgrade, flip one Action card of your choice from side I to side II (it stays in its slot); its improved action is available **from your next action**, while it immediately counts as upgraded for conditions. The current action keeps the strength and kind set at its start; an upgrade gained during it does not add side-II capabilities to it. There are **4 ways to upgrade** an Action card: on the Conservation track, on the Reputation track, and when you gain your second partner zoo or your second partner university. One of them allows you to choose an alternative — so you cannot upgrade all of your Action cards.

requestedparts.part: Donations require Association II and at least one task during that action
requestedparts.evaluation: Complete: Donations require Association II and at least one task during that action. The raw answer supplies this fact semantically, and the cited frozen-summary passage supports it. No fact was borrowed from another answer.
requestedparts.observedanswerquote: A donation is available only with Association II, after performing at least one Association task in that same action; it needs no worker and is limited to one per Association action. Pay the smallest amount still visible and cover that donation space with a player token from your supply to gain 1 conservation. Costs are 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then a repeatable 12-money space; skip spaces blocked at setup. Once all spaces except the last are covered, each later donation costs 12 and places no further token.

summarysupportquote-or-line.quote: - **Side II:** Perform **one or more different** association tasks with one action (1 or 2 of your workers per task, as above). The **total value** of the tasks may not exceed your action's strength (it may be less). Tasks resolve in sequence: workers or other bonuses gained from an earlier task may be used on a later task in this same action. When doing conservation project work you may also play the new Conservation Project card directly **from the display** (within reputation range, paying the folder number as an additional cost; no replenish until turn end). In addition you may make exactly **1 donation**: pay the smallest amount of money still visible in the donation area, cover that space with a player token from your supply, and gain **1 conservation point**. The printed donation costs are **2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10**, then the repeatable **12-money** space; skip spaces blocked at setup. Once all spaces but the last are covered, each subsequent donation costs **12 money** (no further tokens placed). A donation requires having performed at least 1 association task in the same action, needs no worker, and is limited to 1 per Association action.

Card text takes priority over general rules. Cards count their own icons for instant effects and recurring triggers. Only upper-right card icons, partner-zoo/university icons and upper-left water/rock requirements count as zoo icons; left-side conditions and conservation-project icons do not. Doubled icons count twice and trigger matching effects twice. Terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes: touching one water hex in a larger water area gives one adjacency; several edges touching that hex still give only one. Water/rock illustrations on tiles provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.

Terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes: touching one water hex in a larger water area gives one adjacency; several edges touching that hex still give only one. Water/rock illustrations on tiles provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.

requestedparts.part: Venom targets all other eligible zoos with strictly more appeal
requestedparts.evaluation: Complete: Venom targets all other eligible zoos with strictly more appeal. The raw answer supplies this fact semantically, and the cited frozen-summary passage supports it. No fact was borrowed from another answer.
requestedparts.observedanswerquote: Venom affects every other eligible zoo with higher appeal than yours. Hypnosis selects among tied highest-appeal players and targets only slot 1, 2 or 3; self-targeting has no effect. Pilfering 1 targets highest appeal; Pilfering 2 separately targets highest appeal and most conservation (leader must have at least 1 conservation); ties let you choose, and self-targeting has no effect. Constriction affects all other zoos ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation: one token if ahead on one track, two if ahead on both.

summarysupportquote-or-line.quote: **Interactive abilities.** Only zoos with at least five appeal can be affected. If the multiplayer group prefers, replace interactive abilities with the alternative text marked for solo on those cards; this does not require playing the solo mode. The playing animal's appeal may be awarded before or after its ability, so its new appeal normally need not count when deciding the affected player.

- **Venom X:** affect every other zoo with higher appeal than yours, subject to the five-appeal eligibility floor. Place X tokens on cards in the lowest slots (1, then 2, etc.), at most one per card; duplicates return to supply. Using a card with Venom removes its token and avoids all Venom fees that turn. This includes the alternative X-token action if you hold fewer than five X-tokens. Otherwise, if any Venom remains on your cards at turn end, pay two money. If you cannot, undo the turn and choose a different action; you cannot escape the fee by spending all your money. The next break clears unused tokens without effect.

- **Hypnosis:** choose the affected player among ties for highest appeal; if you yourself are the target it has no effect. Choose only a card in the target's **slot 1, 2 or 3**. Execute the targeted Action card using its owner's upgraded/unupgraded side for that whole action. Other action-card upgrade checks use your own cards. You may spend your own X-tokens. Venom and Constriction on the targeted card apply to you and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used. Move the targeted card to slot 1 normally.

- **Pilfering X:** Pilfering 1 affects the zoo with highest appeal. Pilfering 2 affects the zoo with highest appeal **and** the zoo with most conservation points, resolving both targets separately; if the same zoo qualifies for both, pilfer from it twice. Ties for highest appeal or conservation let you choose the affected player; a conservation leader needs at least one conservation point. Self-targeting has no effect. The target chooses to give five money or allow a random hand-card draw (never Final Scoring cards). With no hand cards, give five money; with less than five money, give a card. With neither a card nor five money, give all current money, including zero. Resolve repeated pilferings sequentially; the target may make a different choice each time.

- **Constriction:** affect all other zoos ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation. A zoo ahead on one track receives Constriction 1; ahead on both receives Constriction 2. Place tokens on cards in the highest slots (one on 5, or two on 4 and 5). Never stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. An affected action loses two strength; this applies to each execution of a multiplied action. X-tokens can restore strength. At effective strength zero or below, use enough X-tokens to reach at least one, use the alternative X-token action, or leave the card until it is at least in slot 3. Return the token after acting, or without effect in the break.

summarysupportquote-or-line.quote: Place a newly built standard enclosure **empty side up** (yellow border and size number). Each placement-bonus icon covered is awarded immediately **once**; resolve all covered bonuses before the next building. A standard enclosure turning occupied later does not award its covered placement bonus again.

- **Side II:** Build **as many different buildings as you like** with a **maximum total size equal to the strength** — but never 2 identical buildings in the same Build action. Newly available: **Large Bird Aviary** and **Reptile House** (special enclosures, both size 5, maximum 1 each per zoo, both sides the same). When you build the Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary you may immediately — and only once per building — move **all suitable animals that fit** from standard enclosures into it, choosing separately for each. Build the buildings one after the other, paying for each separately before placing it; take placement bonuses before building the next building, but hold "after finishing" bonuses until the whole Build action is complete. Side II also lets you build on the restricted-icon spaces, so you can completely cover your zoo map: if you cover every space except water and rock spaces (by any effect, not just the Build action), immediately gain **7 appeal**. Unique buildings can never be built with this action — they only come into play via their Sponsor cards.

summarysupportquote-or-line.quote: 7. Randomly determine a start player. Turn order is clockwise.
